QUOTE: allow (`PermissionManager::is_allowed`): a match skips the prompt. It does not grant execution past a deny match, because deny is checked again in `execute`.
VERDICT: MISS
WHY: The answer says allow skips the prompt and that it is used inside `check_approval`. But it never says the allow list is consulted only from `ToolExecutor::check_approval` in a different file. It also never says the allow list does not grant execution.
